git_rationale.root_cause_commit: b5d447e (2026-04-21 17:45 UTC) — chore(claude): sync all uncommitted config, hooks, scripts, sessions, docs. 93-file bulk that rewrote 4 checkpoint hooks without per-file review.
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: The pretool-orchestrator-gate.py is RATE-based (consecutive same-name tool count). At 17:44:54 it correctly fired against the 4th consecutive Bash call (4/3 streak), but the agent issued a Grep call (whitelist tool, resets the streak counter) and reissued the SAME git commit 9 seconds later. The gate had no SEMANTIC component — no subject-pattern check, no multi-subsystem fan-out check, no agent-vs-user authorship check on git commit.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Three new semantic guards: (R4.2) config-surface protection by path; (R4.3) authorship by git verb (agents may only run the blessed `auto-bulk: end-of-cycle commit for ` bridge); (R4.4) multi-subsystem fan-out detection conjunct with AI-bulk subject pattern. Plus R4.1 extends the existing overnight-hook to cover .claude/commands/* (which were missing). Together these close the gap the rate-based gate left open.

dev._permissions_note: No permissions changes required — the 3 new hooks are registered as PreToolUse matchers (not as Bash commands the user invokes). settings.json registration is handled separately by the orchestrator via the update-config skill using the `hooks_to_register` snippet at the top of this report.
implementation_notes: Quality-gate enforced max-30-line functions and max-3 nesting depth, requiring helper extraction in pretool-bulk-commit-detector.py (_file_matches_prefix, _prefixes_for_file split out of _classify_subsystems) and pretool-claude-config-guard.py (_classify_bash_target, _evaluate_write_edit, _evaluate_bash split out of original _evaluate). Functionally identical, just structurally split.
BA spec said hook for R4.4 'recommend `.py` over `.sh` for staged-set parsing' — implemented as .py to match the rest of the family.

R4.3's `_is_agent_context()` always returns True per BA's instruction (line 233 of spec) that the rule applies to BOTH subagents (with `agent_id`) AND main agent. Bypass mechanisms are SEMANTIC (blessed-bridge regex / env var / HEAD-only target), not authorship-based. The `agent_id` field is informational only — the gate fires regardless.

R4.4 is FAIL-OPEN on non-repo CWD (subprocess `git diff --cached --name-only` returns non-zero -> empty staged_files -> early return 0). This means the hook never fires when invoked outside a git repo, which is correct behaviour.

All four hooks fail-open on any uncaught exception (exit 0). This guarantees the harness never wedges due to a hook bug — at the cost of skipping the check when it crashes. Per BA spec critical-safety section.

recommendations: After settings.json registration via update-config skill, QA should re-run AC5-AC8 verification against the LIVE harness (not just synthetic stdin) to confirm hook firing in real Edit/Write/Bash flows. The orchestrator must verify that pretool-claude-config-guard.py does NOT block its own registration — the update-config skill should write to settings.json, which is NOT in .claude/{hooks,commands}/ and therefore NOT subject to this hook.

Watch for false positives in pretool-bulk-commit-detector.py against legitimate human-driven sweeps. The conjunctive check (multi-subsystem AND AI-bulk subject) should be tight enough; if false positives surface, narrow the SUBJECT_PATTERNS rather than the prefix list.

If the orchestrator needs to land a refactor of the .claude/{hooks,commands}/* surface, the user creates `.claude/.hook-refactor-allow` once at project root, the refactor proceeds, then the sentinel is deleted. Document this in the orchestrator workflow if/when the next refactor cycle starts.

R4.3 blessed-bridge regex (`^auto-bulk: end-of-cycle commit for `) must match exactly what /merge produces. Group G1 (merge.md unified) is producing the literal `auto-bulk: end-of-cycle commit for <branch>` per BA spec — confirm cross-group match at integration time.
